solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I run a check on currency for brother

blocks.note: the franc was the currency of France and is still Switzerland's
taken as written
to scan something is to run a check over it

explanation.surface: Someone checks the money before handing it over to a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means following in an across answer, so the two later pieces come after the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A Franciscan is a friar of the order of St Francis, and friars are addressed as Brother.

clue.text: Anticipate no relaxation during trip

indicators.note: what happens during something falls within it, so those pieces go inside

blocks.note: a trip is a stumble, a fall
O is nought, the figure for none
rest is relaxation

explanation.surface: Someone expects to get no break while on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' gives O as nought; both short pieces sit inside the trip just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in anticipation of something so as to prevent it.

clue.text: Volume concealed by a zip that will go under the hammer

definitions.text: that will go under the hammer

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden inside it, so it sits within those letters

blocks.note: taken as written
zip is slang for nothing, nil
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A book hidden in a zipped bag is due to be sold at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go under the hammer' means be auctioned, but read literally it is what an anvil does in a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a smith places metal on to be struck by the hammer.

clue.text: Belligerent allies, we suggested

blocks.note: surface reading: aggressive partners in a war, with us proposing something
setter's reading: the two letters of 'we' are what you get from the centre of the second word of the answer, so the answer's phrase points to them

explanation.surface: We proposed an alliance with warlike partners.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, take the central letters of its second word, and you get W and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central Powers were Germany, Austria-Hungary, Turkey and Bulgaria, allied as combatants in the First World War.

clue.text: Small pine for one, or spruce

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the pine marten is one kind of marten, a weasel-like animal

explanation.surface: A short pine tree, or a spruce, as examples of conifers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine and spruce both look like trees; the pine is the pine marten and spruce is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up and to smarten both mean to make neater in appearance.

clue.text: Suffering pins and needles by the fire

blocks.note: at means beside or by, as in at the door
an ingle is a fireplace, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Someone thaws out by the fire and feels pins and needles.
explanation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling all over, the prickly feeling known as pins and needles.

clue.text: Walk with one in fur, spending time later

indicators.note: what is spent is used up and gone, so the named item is dropped

blocks.note: the stoat, whose winter coat is ermine, is an animal in fur
T is the abbreviation for time; 'later' picks the second of the two Ts

explanation.surface: A stroll alongside someone wearing a fur coat, with the timing put off.
explanation.walkthrough: The fur animal loses its final T to leave STOA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade in ancient Greece, a portico used as a public walkway.

clue.text: One in fifty seven teens not very excitable

indicators.note: not excludes what follows, so the abbreviation it governs is taken out
an excitable crowd will not stay still, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Of a group of fifty, seven teenagers are calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Sailor on motor yacht turning around southern gulf

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the vessel's letters enclose the compass point
turning round makes the letters face the other way, read upwards in this down answer

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
MY is the prefix for a motor yacht, like HMS
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A sailor aboard a motor yacht swings round in a southern bay.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts the sailor on top; the yacht abbreviation is built round the compass point before being turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysm is an old poetic form of abyss, a bottomless gulf or chasm.

clue.text: One painting a capital but not one other city

indicators.note: 'but not' excludes something, so a letter is taken away from the capital

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist elected to the Royal Academy
Vienna is the capital of Austria
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist depicts a capital city, but not another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One painting' is a crossword staple for a member of the Royal Academy; 'other city' is the definition because the capital already named is one city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is an Italian city famed for its mosaics, a second city alongside the capital in the clue.

clue.text: Early stage in imagination

blocks.note: taken as written
fancy is the faculty of imagination

explanation.surface: Something exists only as an early idea in someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the earliest period of life, and by extension the first phase of any development.

clue.text: Defensive position mad character had about source of cash, indeed

indicators.note: to have something about you is to carry it on your person, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: a fort is a fortified defensive position
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
an ATM is a cash machine

explanation.surface: A soldier in a fort has gone mad over money.
explanation.walkthrough: The cash machine goes in after the first letter of the Mad Hatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed and for that matter both add emphasis, meaning as well or in fact.

clue.text: Get high up to install large sort of panel

indicators.note: installing something fits it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to soar is to rise high in the air
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Climb up onto the roof to fit a big solar panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting panels needs a trip up the roof, so the surface sits naturally with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar panel turns sunlight into electricity, so solar describes one kind of panel.

clue.text: Task force for Hull City?

blocks.note: first meaning: a specialist group set loose on a problem, especially to test security
second meaning, whimsically: Hull City football club are nicknamed the Tigers, so their side is literally a team of them

explanation.surface: A special unit is formed to tackle problems in the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull City is an English football club nicknamed the Tigers; the question mark flags that the second sense is a playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger team is a specialist group assembled to attack a particular problem, which is a task force.

clue.text: Hopeful lawyer's second drink? On the wagon, in emergency

indicators.note: one thing on another comes after it in an across answer, so the pieces are swapped from clue order

blocks.note: an ambulance is the vehicle that comes in an emergency
a chaser is a drink taken straight after another, such as beer after a spirit

explanation.surface: A lawyer orders a second drink despite being on the wagon, to cope with a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' looks like the idiom for teetotal, but 'On' is the placing word and the wagon is the ambulance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance chaser is a lawyer who touts for accident victims, hoping to win compensation claims.

clue.text: "Mountain church," a gospel standard

blocks.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
CH is the abbreviation for church
Mark is one of the four gospels

explanation.surface: 'Mountain Church' sounds like the title of a classic gospel song.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a reference point or standard against which other things are measured.

clue.text: Stones are remarkable for echoes

indicators.note: remarkable can be read as re-markable, able to be marked out again in a fresh pattern

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stones are notable for the echoes they give, as in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonates means reverberates, sending sound back as echoes do; it is the verb form here.

clue.text: Unfortunately deaf following last hymn or anthem

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is one gone awry, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad case of someone who could not hear the final hymn or the anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: Land of My Fathers is the English title of Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau, the national anthem of Wales.

clue.text: Wet month abroad? Lots of them

blocks.note: mois is French for month
ten months is a good number of them

explanation.surface: A rainy month overseas, and plenty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' looks like an adjective describing the month, but it is the verb that defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To moisten something is to wet it slightly.

clue.text: For safety switches housing benefit with bachelor — cunning type making the case

definitions.note: read with 'making the case' at the end: the case for safety switches, a noun phrase

indicators.note: a house holds things inside it, so the crafty animal encloses the other pieces

blocks.note: use means benefit, as in 'of no use'
B is the abbreviation for bachelor
the fox is proverbially cunning

explanation.surface: A wily single man claims housing benefit, pleading safety concerns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing benefit' reads as the welfare payment, but housing is the enclosing word; the inner pieces go after the animal's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuse box is the casing that holds a building's fuses or circuit breakers, which are safety switches.

clue.text: Fraudulently obtained title with cash for sport

indicators.note: something obtained by fraud has been fiddled, so the letters are rigged into another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sporting title was won by cheating, with money changing hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletics is the sport of track and field events such as running, jumping and throwing.

clue.text: Apparently embarrassed prosecutor upset poisoner

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are turned upside down in this down answer

blocks.note: someone embarrassed looks red in the face
DA is a District Attorney, the US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A blushing prosecutor is upset by a poisoning case.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, so a poisoner in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Nearly laid out by a tree

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is left off

blocks.note: taken as written
money laid out has been spent

explanation.surface: Someone almost collapsed beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' suggests knocked flat, but here it means paid out; SPENT loses its T and follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar tree known for leaves that tremble in the slightest breeze.

clue.text: Pence and shillings raised in charity work by David

indicators.note: raised means lifted to the top, so in this down answer a letter moves up from the bottom to the head

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for pence
names the S already at the end of the charity word, the one to be moved; S is the abbreviation for shillings
alms are charitable gifts

explanation.surface: Pennies and shillings are collected for a charitable work by someone called David.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of ALMS is the shillings; it is lifted to the top to give SALM, under P. Shillings were pre-decimal British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing many of the Psalms in the Bible.

clue.text: Very keen daughter replacing front of hands-free device

indicators.note: replacing the front means swapping out the first letter for the new one

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
a headset lets you talk without holding a phone

explanation.surface: A daughter is very keen to swap in a hands-free gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dead set on something is to be utterly determined about it, so very keen.

clue.text: Cut and separate a few lines

blocks.note: bit, the past of bite, means cut into with the teeth
to part is to separate

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming a text and splitting off a few lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small acting role with only a handful of lines to speak.

clue.text: For a kiss, cut down strong drink

indicators.note: cutting down the phrase trims its ends so only an inner run of letters survives

blocks.note: the letters sit across the three words, after the F-O and before the final S-S

explanation.surface: Someone gives up strong drink in exchange for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Raki is a potent aniseed spirit from Turkey and the Balkans.

clue.text: One nearest almost slack, very close to death

indicators.note: almost means short of the whole, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
next means nearest in place
remiss means negligent or slack

explanation.surface: The person nearest is nearly idle while someone is dying.
explanation.definitionFit: In extremis is Latin for 'in the furthest reaches', used of someone at the point of death.
